explanations.3: This disables interactive prompts during package installation, so the Docker build won't pause waiting for user input.
explanations.7: This command uses sed (a text editor) to modify Ubuntu's package sources file, adding 'universe' and 'multiverse' repositories where additional packages like fzf are stored.
explanations.14: After installing packages, this deletes the apt cache to reduce the final Docker image size, since we won't need to reinstall anything.
explanations.17: This creates the directory structure /root/.ssh/conf.d and sets its permissions to 700 (only the owner can read, write, execute) for security.
explanations.103: The perl -ne flag means: read each line from the input, automatically strip the newline, and execute the script—this processes the SSH config files line by line.
explanations.104: $sep is a variable being set to a separator string that will later join multiple comment lines together.
explanations.111: This concatenates comment lines into $buf, using the separator; if $buf is empty it adds nothing, otherwise it adds the separator first.
explanations.116: This regex matches a line starting with 'Host' followed by a name (but not wildcards with *), capturing just the alias name.
explanations.132: The padding of 150 spaces ensures that when displaying results in fzf, the description text won't overlap with or wrap into the main search list.
explanations.136: The escaped quotes \' allow single quotes to appear inside a single-quoted Perl string; basically escaping the quote character.
explanations.139: The delimiter tells fzf where to split each result line; ##### is the divider between the alias/hostname and the description.
explanations.146: The {2} is fzf's placeholder for the second field (hostname), which gets piped to Perl to convert color tags like <red> into actual terminal escape codes.
explanations.160: ssh -G outputs the computed SSH configuration for this alias (like the real hostname and username), which we then parse to show the user what will actually run.
explanations.166: This prints a preview of the exact command before executing it, using ANSI codes to make it bold and cyan-colored in the terminal.
explanations.176: This adds a custom shell prompt showing a whale emoji and the username in color, making it visually clear you're inside a Docker container.
